title: Managing a stage boundary: six activities and exception plans
blurb: Name the six managing a stage boundary activities, what each produces, and how the exception plan route differs from a normal stage end.
question: Midway through a stage, the senior user warns that forecast benefits have fallen, though the stage is within tolerance. Which managing a stage boundary activity should handle this?

teach.body: Managing a stage boundary has six activities, all led by the project manager. Two prepare a plan: the next stage plan at a normal stage end, or an exception plan when the board asks for one. Two update the big picture: the project plan and the business case. Then the PM evaluates the stage (end stage report) and requests the next stage. Think: plan, update, update, evaluate, request.

head: Activity
What the PM does
Main output
rows: Plan the next stage near the end of this one
Respond to the board's request after an exception report
Add actuals and the new plan's forecasts
Reflect changes, benefits results and aggregated risk
Brief the board and ask to proceed

steps.label:
Next stage plan

teach.caption: Each update builds on the one before, so the board sees a joined-up picture.

teach.h: Which plan does the PM prepare?
Prepare exception plan: what the PM does
items: Record the board's request for an exception plan in the project log.
Review the PID and update it if required.
Prepare the exception plan to replace the stage plan (or project plan) that can no longer stay within tolerance.
Once the board approves it, that approval marks a stage boundary for the revised stage.

teach.h: Worked scenario: a clinic booking system
teach.body: At Lowmoor Hospital Trust, project manager Hannah Kerr is ending stage 2 of a clinic booking project. Senior user Dr Sam Ade reports that forecast benefits have dropped, although the stage is within tolerance. Hannah handles this in update the business case, revising the benefits forecast in the business case ready for board approval and updating the benefits management approach with the results of benefits actions so far. She then writes the end stage report and, in request next stage, briefs the board on stage 3's people and resources and on a concession granted for one off-specification.

teach.text: Classic traps: (1) A change in forecast benefits is handled in update the business case, NOT by preparing an exception plan. (2) The end stage report is produced in evaluate the stage, not in request next stage or update the project plan. (3) Closure activities are planned in the final stage's plan; there is no separate closure stage. (4) An exception plan replaces a stage or project plan, never a team plan.

items: Six activities: prepare next stage plan, prepare exception plan, update the project plan, update the business case, evaluate the stage, request next stage.
Exception plans: requested by the board, request recorded in the project log, PID reviewed.
Project plan update uses actuals and the new plan's forecasts; revised costs and dates feed the business case.
Business case update covers benefits results and aggregated risk from the project log.
End stage report in evaluate the stage; concessions confirmed in request next stage.

summary: You can now name the six managing a stage boundary activities, say what each produces and choose between the next stage plan and exception plan routes. You can also place benefits changes, end stage reports and concessions in the right activity.

A.q: In which managing a stage boundary activity does the project manager prepare the end stage report?
A.why: Evaluate the stage uses the updated business case, project plan, project log and approaches to prepare the end stage report (manual ch 18).

whyNot.1: Request next stage briefs the board and asks to proceed; the report is already written by then.
whyNot.2: Update the project plan adds actuals and forecasts; it does not produce the end stage report.
whyNot.3: Update the business case revises the business case for board approval.

A.q: Where should the activities needed to close the project be planned?
options: In a separate plan for a closure stage
In the project brief during start-up
In the stage plan for the final stage
In an exception plan for the closure
A.why: Closure activities are planned as part of the stage plan for the final stage, prepared in prepare next stage plan (manual ch 18).

whyNot.0: Closing a project is part of the final stage, not a stage of its own.
whyNot.1: The project brief is produced in starting up a project, long before closure is planned in detail.
whyNot.3: Exception plans respond to forecast tolerance breaches, not planned closure.

A.q: Which activity includes recording the board's request in the project log and reviewing the PID?
A.why: In prepare exception plan the PM records the board's request in the project log and reviews, and if needed updates, the PID (manual ch 18).

whyNot.0: Prepare next stage plan responds to the stage end, not to a board request for an exception plan.
whyNot.1: Evaluate the stage produces the end stage report.
whyNot.2: Request next stage asks the board to proceed to the next stage.

B.q:
Which two statements about managing a stage boundary activities are correct?
1. Update the project plan uses forecasts from the next stage plan or exception plan.
2. An end stage report must accompany every exception plan.
3. The end stage report is prepared in the request next stage activity.
4. Update the business case includes assessing aggregated risk exposure from the project log.
B.why: The project plan update uses the new plan's forecasts (1), and the business case update assesses aggregated risk from the project log (4).

whyNot.0: Statement 2 is false: with an exception plan, an end stage report is needed if the board requires one.
whyNot.2: Both are false: an end stage report with an exception plan depends on the board, and it is produced in evaluate the stage.
whyNot.3: Statement 3 is false: the end stage report is produced in evaluate the stage.

B.q: During stage 3, the senior user reports that forecast benefits have fallen. The stage itself is within tolerance. Which activity should handle this at the boundary?
B.why: A change in benefits forecasts is handled in update the business case, which also updates the benefits management approach ready for board approval (manual ch 18).

whyNot.0: No tolerance is forecast to be exceeded, and the board has not requested an exception plan.
whyNot.1: Evaluate the stage reports on performance; it does not revise the benefits forecasts.
whyNot.2: Update the project plan covers timescales and costs, not benefits.

B.q: In request next stage, what should the project manager confirm to the board about the stage just finishing?
options: The checkpoint reports from each team
The tolerances set for each work package
The exact wording of the project mandate
B.why: In request next stage the PM briefs the board on stage performance, the next stage and resources, readiness, and any concessions for off-specifications (manual ch 18).

whyNot.0: Checkpoint reports are reviewed by the PM during the stage, not presented to the board here.
whyNot.2: Work package tolerances are the PM's concern, not part of the next stage request.
whyNot.3: The mandate was an input to starting up a project and is not reconfirmed here.

C.q: In the evaluate the stage activity, which role is responsible, and which roles are consulted?
options: Executive; the PM and project assurance
Project support; the PM and the team manager
Project manager; TM, support and assurance
Project assurance; the PM and project support
C.why: The official RACI for evaluate the stage makes the PM responsible, with the team manager, project support and project assurance consulted (manual tab 18.2).

whyNot.0: The PM, not the executive, is responsible for evaluating the stage.
whyNot.1: Project support is consulted, not responsible.
whyNot.3: Project assurance is consulted, not responsible.

C.q: Which practice is applied when the quality register is checked for the stage's quality activities, and which when the end stage report is issued?
C.why: Checking the quality register applies the quality practice; creating and issuing the end stage report applies the progress practice (manual tab 18.3).

whyNot.2: The end stage report is a progress product, not a plans product.
whyNot.3: Checking the quality register is the quality practice, not issues.

C.q: Which activity produces revised costs and end dates, and which activity uses them next?
options: Update the business case; used to update the project plan
Evaluate the stage; used to prepare the next stage plan
Request next stage; used to prepare the exception plan
Update the project plan; used to update the business case
C.why: Update the project plan adds actuals and forecasts; any revised costs or end dates are then used when updating the business case (manual ch 18).

whyNot.0: This reverses the flow: the project plan is updated first and feeds the business case.
whyNot.1: The next stage plan comes first and feeds the project plan update, not the other way round.
whyNot.2: Exception plans follow a board request after an exception report, not the next stage request.

reteach.title: The end-of-term review
reteach.question: At the end of a school term, what does a head of year prepare before governors approve next term?

blocks.body: The head of year drafts next term's plan, updates the year plan, checks the budget still adds up, writes a term report and asks the governors to approve next term. If a crisis means the current term can't finish as planned, the governors ask for a recovery plan instead. Same six activities: next stage plan or exception plan, two updates, evaluate, request.

blocks.text: A recovery plan (exception plan) is only prepared when the governors (board) ask for one after being warned (exception report).

explain.body: The plan for the next stage is produced near the end of the current stage. For the final stage, it includes the closure activities.

test.q: When is the stage plan for the next stage produced?
options: During initiation, with the project plan
Near the end of the current stage
After the board authorizes the next stage
test.why: Prepare next stage plan produces the plan near the end of the current stage (manual ch 18).

whyNot.0: Initiation produces the project plan; delivery stage plans are produced at each boundary.
whyNot.2: The board needs the plan in order to authorize the stage.
whyNot.3: Starting up a project produces the initiation stage plan, not later stage plans.

explain.body: Exception plans are requested by the board in response to an exception report. The PM records the request, reviews the PID and prepares the plan.

test.q: What triggers the prepare exception plan activity?
options: A board request after an exception report
A late checkpoint report from a team manager
A change in the forecast project benefits
The approaching end of the final stage
test.why: Exception plans are requested by the project board in response to an exception report (manual ch 18).

whyNot.1: A late checkpoint report is handled by the PM in controlling a stage.
whyNot.2: Benefits forecast changes are handled in update the business case.
whyNot.3: The end of the final stage leads to closing a project.

explain.body: The PM reflects external and project changes, updates the benefits management approach with results of benefits actions, and assesses aggregated risk from the project log.

test.q: In update the business case, which product is updated with the results of benefits actions taken during the stage?
test.why: Update the business case updates the benefits management approach with the results of benefits management actions (manual ch 18).

whyNot.0: The quality management approach covers quality procedures, not benefits results.
whyNot.1: Work package descriptions belong to controlling a stage.
whyNot.3: The communication management approach covers who receives what information and when.

explain.body: The PM briefs the board on the current stage's performance, an overview of the next stage, the people and resources needed and readiness to proceed, plus any concessions.

test.q: Which activity briefs the board on the next stage's people and resources and confirms readiness to proceed?
test.why: Request next stage briefs the board on stage performance, the next stage, people and resources, and readiness to proceed (manual ch 18).

whyNot.0: Evaluate the stage prepares the end stage report.
whyNot.1: Update the project plan adds actuals and forecasts.
whyNot.2: Prepare next stage plan produces the plan, but the briefing happens in request next stage.
